name: Plenitude
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
industry: energy retail, renewables and EV charging
desc: Sells gas and electricity to about 10 million customers, produces renewable power and runs Be Charge EV charging points.
ownership: subsidiary of Eni; Energy Infrastructure Partners holds about 10% (since March 2025)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 10,168 million in 2025; EIP bought about 7.6% in March 2024, raised to 10% in March 2025
markets: Retail customers in Italy, France, Portugal, Greece, Spain and Slovenia; renewables in Europe, US, Colombia, Kazakhstan and Australia; charging in eight European countries
rationale: Consumer-facing European energy and EV-charging brand selling to 10 million households; F1's energy-transition storyline suits its retail and Be Charge marketing.

name: JioStar
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: Indian media company running more than 100 TV channels and the JioHotstar streaming platform, with major cricket rights.
ownership: subsidiary of Reliance Industries (16.34% directly plus 46.82% via Viacom18, about 63%); Disney holds 36.84%
capacity_detail: Viacom18-Disney Star merger valued at USD 8.5 billion, completed 14 November 2024; revenue INR 260 billion (USD 2.8bn) FY2024
markets: India: over 100 TV channels and JioHotstar streaming; IPL and other cricket and sports media rights
rationale: India's dominant sports broadcaster and streamer could use F1 partnership or rights to grow JioHotstar's premium motorsport audience.

name: Vale Base Metals
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: Vale's nickel and copper mining business with operations in Canada, Indonesia and New Caledonia, legally Vale Canada Limited.
ownership: subsidiary of Vale; Manara Minerals (Ma'aden and PIF) about 10%, Engine No. 1 about 3%
capacity_detail: Sold 13% to Manara Minerals and Engine No. 1 for USD 3.4 billion (agreed July 2023)
markets: Mines and plants in Canada (Ontario, Manitoba, Newfoundland and Labrador), Indonesia and New Caledonia; global metals sales
rationale: Nickel and copper supplier to EV batteries could use F1's sustainability and electrification story to court carmakers and investors.

name: 11st
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: South Korean online shopping marketplace, majority-owned by SK Square and being transferred to SK Planet in 2025.
ownership: subsidiary of SK Square (80.3%), being sold to SK Planet (86.3% owned by SK Square); Nile Holdings (H&Q Korea, NPS, Saemaul Geumgo) held 18.2%
capacity_detail: Raised KRW 500 billion from Nile Holdings (H&Q Korea, National Pension Service, Saemaul Geumgo) in 2018
markets: South Korea online retail, linked with SK Planet's OK Cashback loyalty programme
rationale: Korean e-commerce brand fighting Coupang could use F1's growing Korean fanbase for awareness, though finances are under pressure.

name: IM Motors
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: Chinese premium electric car brand (Zhiji) founded in 2020 by SAIC with Alibaba and Zhangjiang Hi-Tech.
ownership: subsidiary of SAIC Motor (54%); Alibaba Group 18%, Zhangjiang Hi-Tech 18%
capacity_detail: Raised over RMB 8 billion Series B equity (March 2024) led by Bank of China Asset Management, with CATL, Momenta and others
markets: China, with planned sales in Mexico, Middle East, South America, Southeast Asia and Europe alongside MG dealers
rationale: Premium Chinese EV brand expanding into Europe and the Middle East via MG showrooms needs global awareness that F1 delivers.

name: Piccoma
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: Japanese digital comic app selling manga and webtoon chapters, operated by Kakao Piccoma Corp., formerly Kakao Japan.
ownership: subsidiary of Kakao (via Kakao Piccoma Corp.); Anchor Equity Partners and overseas sovereign funds invested in 2021
capacity_detail: Kakao Japan raised about KRW 600 billion from Anchor Equity Partners and overseas sovereign wealth funds at KRW 8.8 trillion valuation (May 2021)
markets: Japan, the world's largest manga market; European service in France closed September 2024
rationale: Japan's top-grossing manga app could tie into F1's Suzuka audience and anime-style content, though its market is mainly domestic.

name: KT Cloud
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: South Korean cloud computing and internet data centre operator spun out of KT, building AI infrastructure services.
ownership: subsidiary of KT Corp.; IMM Credit & Solutions holds a minority stake (2023)
capacity_detail: Raised KRW 600 billion (about USD 452M) from IMM Credit & Solutions in May 2023 at KRW 4.6 trillion corporate value; sales over KRW 550 billion in 2022
markets: South Korean public, financial and enterprise cloud and data centre customers; reviewing data centres in Southeast Asia
rationale: AI-cloud and data-centre brand could showcase computing performance through F1 technology partnerships, as rival cloud providers already do.

name: JSW One Platforms
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: B2B e-commerce platform selling steel, cement and building materials to small manufacturers and homebuilders, with credit services.
ownership: subsidiary of JSW Group (described as a unit of JSW Group); JSW Steel, Mitsui, Principal Asset Management and OneUp invested
capacity_detail: Raised INR 340 crore at USD 1 billion valuation (May 2025); operating income about INR 1,398 crore FY24
markets: Indian MSME manufacturers and individual home builders through JSW One MSME and JSW One Homes
rationale: Mainly domestic B2B platform; F1 fit is weak beyond JSW group hospitality and brand building among Indian businesses.
parent_listed: not listed (group; JSW Steel is listed)

name: stc Bank
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: Saudi digital bank, formerly the stc pay payments wallet, offering transfers to over 200 countries via Western Union.
ownership: subsidiary of stc Group; Western Union holds 15%
capacity_detail: Western Union bought 15% for USD 200 million (signed Nov 2020 at SAR 5bn valuation, completed Oct 2021)
markets: Saudi Arabia retail digital banking and payments; international remittances to over 200 countries
rationale: Saudi digital bank whose parent already partners F1; the Jeddah Grand Prix offers a natural home-market activation for its youthful customer base.

name: Lufthansa Technik
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: Provides maintenance, repair and overhaul for aircraft, engines and components to over 800 airline and operator customers worldwide.
ownership: subsidiary of Lufthansa Group
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 6.8 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 14%; adjusted EBIT EUR 515 million
markets: Sites in Germany, wider Europe, the US, Puerto Rico, China, Hong Kong, India, Malaysia, Philippines and UAE; 800+ customers
rationale: Engineering-led MRO brand serving global airlines could use F1's precision-engineering image for B2B hospitality and technical recruitment.

name: Tata Play
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: Indian direct-to-home satellite television and content distribution service with about a third of India's DTH subscribers.
ownership: subsidiary of Tata Group (70%); Disney India 30%; Temasek bought 10% from Tata in 2008
capacity_detail: Revenue INR 5,741 crore (about USD 610 million) in 2026
markets: India: 21.3 million DTH subscribers (March 2023), 32.65% of the market
rationale: Indian pay-TV distributor in a declining market; F1 content or sponsorship could help retain premium sports-viewing households.

name: Jio-bp
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: Indian fuel and mobility retailer, legally Reliance BP Mobility, operating over 1,700 retail fuel outlets across India.
ownership: subsidiary of Reliance Industries (51%); bp 49%
capacity_detail: Revenue INR 63,840 crore (USD 6.8 billion) in 2026
markets: India: over 1,700 retail fuel outlets plus mobility services
rationale: Consumer fuel brand competing with state retailers; co-owner bp's F1 links and Castrol-style fuel marketing make motorsport a natural fit.

name: GeniTech (Shenji)
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: NIO's chip unit Anhui Shenji (GeniTech), designer of the 5-nanometre NX9031 autonomous-driving chip used in NIO vehicles.
ownership: subsidiary of NIO (62.7% after Feb 2026 round); Hefei state capital and IDG Capital among investors
capacity_detail: First outside round raised over RMB 2.2 billion (about USD 318M) at post-money valuation near RMB 10 billion (about USD 1.4bn), Feb 2026
markets: Supplies NIO vehicles in China; licenses smart-driving technology through a JV with Axera and OmniVision

signals.raise: Series A of over RMB 2.2bn from Hefei state funds and IDG (Feb 2026; https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-02-28/nio-chip-unit-raises-318-million-at-nearly-14-billion-valuation-102417691.html)

rationale: B2B automotive chip designer seeking outside carmaker customers; F1 technical branding is possible but brand-led payoff is limited.

name: Olive Young
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: South Korea's leading health and beauty store chain with over 1,300 stores, online global mall and first US store.
ownership: subsidiary of CJ Group (CJ Olive Young Corporation)
capacity_detail: Sales KRW 5.8335 trillion in 2025, up 21.8%; operating profit KRW 744.7 billion
markets: South Korea stores and online, global online mall, first US store in Pasadena (May 2026), Sephora partnership

signals.regions: Opened first US store in Pasadena, California (May 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olive_Young_(company))

rationale: K-beauty retailer expanding into the US with Sephora could use F1's young, growing female and American fanbase to build global awareness.

name: Starbucks Korea (SCK Company)
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: SCK Company operates Starbucks coffee shops in South Korea, about 2,009 stores at end-2024, the third-largest Starbucks market.
ownership: subsidiary of E-mart (67.5%); remaining 32.5% held by a Singapore investor
capacity_detail: Annual sales estimated to pass KRW 3 trillion for the first time in 2024; Q2 2026 sales KRW 747.3 billion
markets: South Korea: 2,009 Starbucks stores at end-2024
rationale: Large Korean coffee chain recovering from a 2026 marketing backlash; licensed brand limits independent global sponsorship, so domestic F1 activations only.

name: Tata AIA Life
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: Indian life insurer, a joint venture of Tata Sons and Hong Kong's AIA Group, selling protection and savings policies.
ownership: subsidiary of Tata Sons (51%); AIA Group 49%
capacity_detail: Revenue INR 25,692 crore (about USD 2.7 billion) in 2024; net income INR 1,314 crore
markets: India: individual and group life insurance sold through agents, banks and online
rationale: Life insurer targeting India's affluent professionals; F1's rising Indian audience offers premium brand association, though rivals favour cricket.

name: Tata AIG
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: Indian general insurer owned by Tata Sons and AIG, selling motor, health, travel, property and commercial insurance.
ownership: subsidiary of Tata Sons (74%); American International Group 26%
capacity_detail: Revenue INR 11,408 crore (about USD 1.3 billion) in 2024 per the article's financials section (infobox gives INR 15,424 crore)
markets: India: motor, health, travel, home and commercial insurance
rationale: Major Indian motor insurer; F1's car-centric audience and road-safety messaging suit its motor and travel insurance marketing.

name: Mahindra Last Mile Mobility
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: Mahindra & Mahindra's electric three-wheeler and last-mile commercial vehicle subsidiary, backed by IFC, India-Japan Fund and Lightrock.
ownership: subsidiary of Mahindra & Mahindra (78.11% falling to 75.79%); IFC, India-Japan Fund and Lightrock minority
capacity_detail: Raised USD 33 million led by Lightrock at about USD 1.1 billion post-money valuation (July 2026)
markets: India last-mile cargo and passenger electric three-wheeler market

signals.raise: USD 33M led by Lightrock at USD 1.1bn valuation (Jul 2026; https://rnm.in/blog/india-investment-deals-july-2026-pe-vc-ma-updates/)

rationale: Commercial EV three-wheeler maker selling to Indian fleet operators; F1 relevance is low beyond Mahindra group electrification messaging.

name: Shanghai Mahexin Technology (Li Auto chip unit)
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: Li Auto's in-house chip design subsidiary, developing vehicle chips and planning external sales beyond automotive.
ownership: subsidiary of Li Auto (about 74.01% after Series A); Hangzhou Jingtao, Bessemer Venture Partners, Huaye Tiancheng, Qijing Chuangtan minority
capacity_detail: Series A of RMB 1.625 billion (RMB 625 million from outside investors) at RMB 17.1 billion post-money valuation if a further RMB 500 million option is exercised (Oct 2026)
markets: Supplies Li Auto vehicles in China; plans external chip sales

signals.raise: Series A RMB 1.625bn incl. RMB 625M from outside investors (Oct 2026; https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/li-auto-s-chip-subsidiary-raises-1-625-billion-rmb-in-series-a-valued-at-17-1-billion-rmb-post-funding)

rationale: B2B automotive chip unit with little consumer brand; F1 link would serve only technical credibility with future carmaker customers.

name: Rakuten Card
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: Japanese credit card issuer of the Rakuten ecosystem, based in Minato-ku, Tokyo, with insurance and Rakuten Edy subsidiaries.
ownership: subsidiary of Rakuten Group (about 85% after 14.99% transfer to Mizuho Financial Group, Dec 2024)
capacity_detail: Rakuten Group transferred 14.99% to Mizuho FG for JPY 164,997 million (about USD 1.1bn), executed December 2024; consolidated revenue JPY 406,350 million in 2023
markets: Japan consumer credit cards and payments, insurance and Rakuten Edy e-money
rationale: Rakuten's biggest card brand could extend the group's Ferrari F1 deal into card-member perks and Japanese Grand Prix promotions.

name: Swiss International Air Lines
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: Switzerland's flag-carrier airline, flying 21.4 million passengers to about 120 destinations from Zurich and Geneva.
ownership: subsidiary of Lufthansa Group (fully owned)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 6,481 million in 2025; 21.4 million passengers
markets: Flights from Switzerland to about 120 destinations across Europe, North America, Asia, Africa and the Middle East
rationale: Premium Swiss airline brand; rivals Qatar Airways and Etihad use F1, and premium travellers match its long-haul business-class focus.

name: Sadia Halal
group: Subsidiaries with their own outside investors
desc: MBRF's halal food business selling Sadia-branded products, in partnership with Saudi Arabia's PIF-owned Halal Products Development Company.
ownership: subsidiary of MBRF (global operator); Halal Products Development Company (owned by PIF) minority stake of 10-20%, possibly rising to 40%
capacity_detail: Minority partnership with PIF's HPDC valued Sadia Halal at about USD 2.07 billion (SAR 8bn); HPDC investing about USD 268M; closed May 2026
markets: Halal food production and trade centred on Saudi Arabia and the Gulf

signals.raise: HPDC (PIF) minority investment of about USD 268M at USD 2.07bn valuation (May 2026; https://saudifoodtech.sa/newsletters/steak/newsletters-steak-brief-01-en/)
signals.ipo: IPO referenced as deadline for HPDC instalments (2026; https://saudifoodtech.sa/newsletters/steak/newsletters-steak-brief-01-en/)

rationale: Consumer food brand building a Saudi halal hub before an IPO; the Saudi and Gulf Grands Prix offer regional brand-building with PIF alignment.
